paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Gibeonites fooled Israel because Israel took a taste test and skipped the one step that mattered. Joshua 9:14 says the men of Israel "sampled their provisions but did not seek the counsel of the LORD." The bread looked moldy, the sandals looked worn, and every bit of the evidence looked convincing. But looking convincing and being true are two different things, and only God can tell them apart.

Now watch what happens next, because this part gets me. The leaders had sworn an oath by the LORD, the God of Israel, so even after the truth came out, they kept their word (Joshua 9:18-21). The whole congregation grumbled, but the leaders held steady. I think that's a hard kind of faithfulness, the kind that keeps a promise even when it costs you something.

So here's what I'd take to your own kitchen, baker. Before you sign, say yes or make a big move, ask God first, even when the situation looks as clear as day. Hold your promises tight, too, because your word matters to Him. And if you do end up with a mess on your hands, take heart. This story isn't over, and the oven is still on.
